title: Phase 2B: Collection search screen + filter widgets
description: Build the Collection Search UI: query bar, structured filter panel (WUBRG pips, card-type select, price slider, set picker, rarity, treatment toggles), card tile, mana pip widget, results grid. Desktop filter rail + mobile bottom sheet.
close_reason: Phase 2 complete: query engine + search UI integrated

title: Phase 2A: Query parser, AST, and SQL compiler
description: Build the query engine: recursive descent parser for Scryfall-subset grammar, AST node types, drift SQL compiler, and query engine facade. Covers D5 grammar subset.
close_reason: Phase 2 complete: query engine + search UI integrated

title: Phase 1: Corpus pipeline + drift-on-web spike
description: Build Scryfall download/parse/insert pipeline with drift/SQLite. Prove OPFS persistence on web. Critical path — architecture depends on this.

title: Phase 0: Project bootstrap and Flutter scaffold
description: Initialize Flutter project, establish directory structure, add dependencies, create theme from STYLE_GUIDE.md. Clean up stale .idea/ metadata. Push docs/wireframes and scaffold to origin.

title: Add color identity (id:) filter to filter panel UI
description: The query engine already supports id: for color identity searches, but the filter panel UI only exposes c: (colors). Need to add an identity section or toggle between color/identity mode. Important for cards like Ghostfire (colorless but red identity).

title: Add 'in collection' filter (distinct from idle-only)
description: Currently there's only an 'idle only' toggle (unused:true). Users also need a way to filter to 'cards I own' without the idle constraint. Add a have: or owned: predicate that checks against the user collection table. Depends on Phase 3 user DB.

title: is:borderless returns no results
description: The is:borderless query filter returns empty results. The frameEffects column stores Scryfall frame_effects values — need to verify if 'borderless' is actually stored there or if it's a separate field (border_color). Investigate Scryfall data and fix the compiler.

title: Add debug corpus mode for faster dev/test iteration
description: The full Scryfall Default Cards download is ~150MB and takes 1-2 minutes to import on web. For development and testing, add a way to import a smaller corpus instead. Options: (1) use Scryfall's oracle_cards bulk data (~15MB, one printing per card) via a compile-time flag or Settings toggle, (2) provide a pre-built small fixture JSON with ~1000 cards. The debug mode should be opt-in and clearly labeled so users don't accidentally use it in production. Consider a --dart-define=DEBUG_CORPUS=true flag or a developer toggle in Settings.

title: Add COOP/COEP headers for OPFS storage backend
description: Drift falls back from OPFS to SharedIndexedDb because the browser is missing dedicatedWorkersInSharedWorkers and sharedArrayBuffers features. These require Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp headers. Need to: (1) add a custom Flutter dev server config or proxy that sets these headers for local dev, (2) update the GitHub Pages deploy workflow to serve these headers, (3) verify drift reports OPFS as the storage implementation after the fix. OPFS is significantly faster for bulk inserts than IndexedDB — this should cut import time substantially.

title: Improve onboarding progress feedback with phase labels and card count
description: The onboarding download progress currently just says 'downloading...' for the entire import, which takes 1-2 minutes. The actual phases are: 1) Resolving download URL, 2) Downloading ~150MB, 3) Parsing JSON + inserting cards into DB. The status text and progress bar should reflect which phase is active, and show a card count during the parse/insert phase (e.g. 'Inserting cards... 45,000 / ~100,000'). This would prevent users from thinking the app is stuck.

title: Phase 1: App shell + navigation + onboarding UI
description: Build desktop sidebar and mobile bottom nav shell, onboarding screen with download progress UI, data freshness banner.

title: Support multiple set codes in query (s:mh2,mh3 or s:mh2 OR s:mh3)
description: Currently s: only supports a single set code. Users should be able to search across multiple sets. Options: support comma-separated values in s: field, or rely on OR groups (s:mh2 OR s:mh3). May need parser changes if comma syntax is desired.
